title: The landing lock is fair, a code item lands in one run, and claims and dead runs do not block
goal: waiters of the clone's landing lock take it in the order they asked, so the landing that has waited longest is next and none ends refused at step landing lock while younger waiters pass it; a ticket of a process that died is skipped, so a dead waiter holds nobody up; land finds the merge of code/ID on the integration main when the branch is already gone from the remote after the push, so the first pass ends with that merge to wait for and the same run goes on to its second pass; land stops with no tip only when neither the branch nor its merge is there; a land run that waited for a code item's merge request ends with a land.end row that names the code lane; ops prints a landing's land.end row after its last land.step row when the two share a timestamp; kbmon's landing queue lists only the items whose land process runs, so a land that died leaves no queue entry that peers read as a held lock or a waiter; claim resolves the operator before it takes the claims-ledger lock; claim makes no coord call inside the lock that can outlast the lock's stale age, so a slow coord or claude never lets a waiting claim clear a live lock; claim in a checkout whose git dir is not writable claims the item as before the ledger lock, so ledger_lock's OSError on creating the lock file no longer refuses the claim itself; the claim prints a warning that says the claims ledger was not recorded; the kb-sprint skill's plan step 6 tells the planner that a claim or lock race fix's checks plant each case the goal's another session covers: the same key and a different key
